# WaitFeed

> While your agent works, a slim news ticker appears above the prompt or in
> the statusline.
> You start typing — it vanishes. `/news` opens the fullscreen reader.
> **No ads. No accounts. No server. No API keys.**

Every card is real news — a headline, a short blurb from the fetched data,
and the origin link underneath. Nothing is invented, and a dead channel
never empties the rotation — recent items are carried over for 36 hours.

## Hosts

One package, three terminal AI coding agents:

- **[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai)** — the original home: the ticker lives
  above the prompt, `/news` opens the fullscreen reader, and each card gets
  a short story written **only** from the fetched description (never
  invented) by your own session's model. The story pool holds 60 ready
  cards so the ticker never loops the same handful.
- **[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)** — the same card in the
  statusline row: instant on Enter, gone the moment you press **Esc** or the
  agent waits on you, quiet on the splash screen. Headline mode (the feed's
  own description — this host has no keyless LLM path); full behavior in
  [`claude/README.md`](claude/README.md).
- **Google Antigravity (AGY)** — the same card in the agent statusline,
  shown while the agent is working (`working`/`tool_use`/`reviewing`) and
  quiet on the splash screen and idle states.

All three share one data dir (`~/.config/waitfeed/`): one shared fetch
pipeline feeds every agent on the machine (a cycle lock serializes hosts),
and a channel you disable anywhere is disabled everywhere.

## Install

Run the interactive setup wizard — it detects which of the three agents are
installed and wires each one (idempotent — re-running never duplicates):

```bash
npx waitfeed init
```

To configure OpenCode by hand, add `waitfeed` to `plugins` in your
`opencode.json(c)`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": ["waitfeed"]
}
```

## Uninstall

```bash
npx waitfeed remove
```

Removes the integration from every agent — the config entries and the
staged bundle files — and then deletes `~/.config/waitfeed/` (the news
cache and your channel choices). Nothing of WaitFeed is left configured
anywhere; `npx waitfeed init` afterwards starts the onboarding fresh.

- Keep the data folder but remove the integrations:
  `npx waitfeed remove --keep-data`.
- Plain `npm uninstall waitfeed` only removes the npm package — it never
  touches the agent integrations, which is exactly what `remove` is for.
  If you installed the package globally, finish with
  `npm uninstall -g waitfeed`.

## Use

**OpenCode**

- **During a run**, the ticker rotates story cards while the agent works.
- **`/news`** opens the reader: up/down (or j/k) move, **Enter** opens the
  selected link, keys **1–4** toggle channels (Hacker News · dev.to ·
  GitHub trending · Reddit r/programming), **esc** closes.
- Channel switches save instantly to `~/.config/waitfeed/config.json`; a
  disabled channel is not even contacted by the next fetch cycle.
- Add your own RSS/Atom URLs in the same file (`"rssUrls": [...]`, max 10) —
  they always run and show with an `RSS` badge.

**Claude Code** (full behavior in [`claude/README.md`](claude/README.md))

- The card appears in the statusline the moment you submit a prompt, and
  hides when the turn ends, when the agent waits on a question or a
  permission, or when you press **Esc** to interrupt.
- Every busy↔idle transition repaints **instantly** (a settings flip, not
  the refresh tick); Esc hides within milliseconds via the transcript
  watcher.
- Channels are shared with OpenCode; without it, toggle them by editing
  `~/.config/waitfeed/config.json`.

**Antigravity (AGY)**

- Start `agy` — the statusline ticker rotates while the agent works.
- Channels are shared with OpenCode, exactly as above.

## Configuration

`~/.config/waitfeed/config.json` (shared by every host):

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sources` | all on | per-channel switches: `hn`, `devto`, `github`, `reddit` |
| `rssUrls` | `[]` | your own RSS/Atom feeds |
| `dwellSeconds` | `20` | card hold time during a run (5–120s) |
| `setupDone` | `false` | set by your first keypress inside the reader |

Data lives locally in `~/.config/waitfeed/`. The only network calls are to the
feed URLs you keep enabled, once every 30 minutes. Nothing else ever leaves
your machine.

## Honest limits

- Items whose fetched description is too thin to write a real story from stay
  invisible instead of getting a padded look-alike (story cards — OpenCode).
- If the story layer is unavailable, OpenCode's whole view flips to
  plain-headline mode until the next cycle re-probes — the two looks are
  never mixed.
- Claude Code and Antigravity always render headline mode (headline +
  description + link): those hosts have no keyless LLM path, and the
  project bans API keys.
- First run: the ticker stays honestly empty for a few seconds until the
  first stories land.

## Requirements

- One or more of: **OpenCode** (v2 plugin API — npm plugin packages load via
  `plugins` in `opencode.json(c)`), **Claude Code** (statusLine + hooks), or
  **Google Antigravity** (`agy` statusline).
- Node 20+ (npm may warn about `@opentui/core` engine ranges — that is
  OpenCode's own TUI dependency and runs inside OpenCode's runtime;
  installation via `npm install` is not the intended use)

## Dependency notes

All runtime dependencies are pinned to **exact versions** — the tree this
package was developed, tested, and audit-cleared against. Bumps happen
deliberately, at release time.

Two things are inherited from the OpenCode adapter's chain
(`@opencode/plugin`) and are outside this package's control:

- A plain `npm install waitfeed` (or `npm ls`) can print `seroval`/`solid-js`
  advisories from inside the `@opencode/plugin` package's own dependency
  subtree. The ticker's usage path never invokes the deserialization APIs in
  question; it renders text nodes. The fix belongs upstream (OpenCode bumping
  its `solid-js`), and this package re-checks the audit at every release.
- The `@opencode/plugin` dependency chain pulls `undici@8` on consumer
  installs; waitfeed's own dev tree pins `undici` to the Node 20-compatible
  6.x via its root override (overrides cannot travel with a published
  package). Loading through OpenCode is verified at each release.

# WaitFeed — Claude Code Mod (the `/news` pane + prompt-band ticker)

> While your Claude Code agent works: the rotating news card in the band
> above the prompt; `/news` opens a pane of pressable headlines — a press
> opens the link and marks the row read. Keyless, local, observational.

This directory is a Claude Code **mod**: a plugin whose hooks module draws
in the interface. `npx waitfeed init` stages it into
`~/.claude/waitfeed/claude-mod/` and points `env.CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS`
in `~/.claude/settings.json` at it — the env-var route the mods docs list
for launches where a `--plugin-dir` flag is impossible (`;`-separated on
Windows). `npx waitfeed remove` takes both back out; foreign plugin dirs
survive.

## What it draws

| Render site | What |
| --- | --- |
| `AbovePrompt` band | The dwell-correct rotating card — badge, headline, `▲ score · age`, description — **only while the agent executes** (`e.props.isWorking`). Idle it draws nothing (`next(e)`) — the shared quiet-at-idle rule. |
| `/news` pane | Opened by the `news` command (`immediate: true` lets it open mid-turn; `focus: true` + `closeOnEscape: true`). A dim hint bar leads it — `↑/↓ move · Enter open · Esc close` — and it opens with the **first UPCOMING row focused** (the docs' focus prop, set only there; the VS Code extension draws as without). One **single line per headline** (`[src] Title · ▲ score · 2h  read 3m` — the description stays in the cache); `UPCOMING — new to you` first, then `SEEN — already brought to you`. Pressing a row opens the link and marks it read: Windows via `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler` (single program, args verbatim) with `start /c` as the fallback; macOS `open` → Linux `xdg-open`. |

Both sites render FROM the shared data; nothing here fetches.

## The sticky-cursor pane (how the keys behave)

The pane is a **sticky-cursor list** — the vim/fzf/IRC-log contract: the
cursor never leaves view; the window content slips under it one row, only
when it would cross an edge. Content follows the cursor, never the other
way round. Built on the mods events in the build's type declarations
(`claude-code.d.ts`, the 2.1.277 copy — re-verify on your build with
`/plugin-types` after updates):

- **↑ / ↓** inside the pane **move the cursor** one pressable row, across
  both piles (the row the ring sits on draws inverted). Every step re-
  reveals the ring with `$.ui.scroll({ block: 'nearest' })`, so the window
  slides exactly when the cursor reaches its edge — never earlier.
- **The wheel** inside the pane moves the cursor too — this reader has no
  content scrolling; "moves summed in flight" break to at most one step
  per event burst.
- **Enter** opens the focused row's link and marks it read; **Esc** closes
  the pane. **Tab** also walks rows, and mouse clicks work in fullscreen
  rendering — all host-native.
- **PageUp / PageDown / Home / End keep scrolling the window** — the one
  documented scroll path left to them; the translator passes them through.
- At either list edge the extra press is a no-op. A refresh that reshapes
  the piles may reseat the cursor to the first drawn row.
- Fail-soft everywhere: a denied ring move or a thrown hook falls back to
  `next(e)` — the host's own scroll — via `.catch` on both gating hooks.

A mod cannot bind Tab or the arrow keys (`interface.md`: "A mod can't bind
Tab or the arrow keys to anything else") — no key is intercepted here;
`ui.scroll` is consumed **per the hook contract** ("a hook kept the
window") and re-expressed as cursor moves.

## Data rules (host parity)

- The card and the pane read `~/.config/waitfeed/cache.json` — the same
  fetch → enrich → junk-drop → cache pipeline the OpenCode plugin and the
  statusline scheduler run. The band's 20 s dwell timer re-reads the file
  and advances the card; `$.ui.invalidate('ui.render')` asks for redraws.
- The seen ledger is the SHARED `~/.config/waitfeed/reader-state.json`
  (`{ read, glanced }`, key = `url || id`, trimmed + lowercased; marks age
  out at 36 h with the cache window). One mark of either kind puts an item
  in SEEN, so the piles match across hosts.
- Honesty of marks: `read` = you pressed the row (its time is the row's
  only label); `glanced` = a dwell on a ticker — written by hosts that
  record it, never claimed by a press here.
- `$.fs.write` is not atomic (mods docs). The OpenCode TUI owns the atomic
  write path; this mod re-reads the ledger immediately before writing —
  the docs' own advice for values several sessions change — so a
  concurrent mark survives and a race loses at most one mark.

## Version gate

Needs Claude Code **v2.1.295 or later** (rows of buttons with children).
Verified 2026-10-29 on 2.1.311 against the mods docs fetched the same day
(`create.md`, `interface.md`, `api.md`, `reference.md`). The hooks module
obeys every static-analysis rule: string-literal event names, `$` calls in
full, `$` passed only to top-level functions of the same file, and no
module paths at all — file/env/process/clock access goes through the mods
API because a hooks module has no Node.js APIs of its own.

## Development

- Validate: `claude plugin validate packages/waitfeed/claude-mod`
- Try without staging: `claude --plugin-dir packages/waitfeed/claude-mod`
- After a session opened the pane once, it reopens from 110 columns; before
  that a mod-opened pane wants 144. Opening it from `/news` always works.
- Tests: `tests/claude-mod.test.ts` (source contract), the `claude` blocks
  in `tests/cli.test.ts` (staging + removal). Run the full suite from the
  repo root: `npx vitest run`.

The mod is strictly observational: it draws, and it never touches prompts,
tools, or agent behavior.

# WaitFeed — Claude Code Adapter

> While your Claude Code agent works: a slim news card in the statusline row —
> keyless, local, observational, quiet when idle.

## What it renders

The `statusLine` command reads the same shared cache as every other WaitFeed
host (`~/.config/waitfeed/cache.json`) and prints the dwell-correct news card
in the proven AGY layout:

```
▍ [HN] Alpha headline                      ▲ 120 · 2h
Clean fed description snippet, wrapped.    ← ≤3 rows, from the fed data
github.com/…/the-story                     ← OSC 8 link: ctrl+click opens it
```

- Headline mode only (fed data; no LLM stories — the project bans API keys).
- The card advances on wall-clock dwell (20s default), persisted in
  `claude-rotation.json` — redraws inside one dwell window show the same card.

## Fitting the host field (no cut-offs)

Claude Code renders the statusline in a field narrower than the `COLUMNS` it
exports (~3 columns of right inset) and truncates overflow with `…`
(anthropics/claude-code#81454, #69967). The runner therefore right-justifies
every row to `COLUMNS − 4` (the same reserve ccstatusline ships) and wraps
long headlines across lines instead of truncating: no headline, metadata,
score, or time indicator is ever cut off at the corner.

## Busy/idle (AGY parity)

The statusline payload carries no busy flag, so an activity ledger
(`claude-activity.json`, per Claude session) decides when the card shows —
driven entirely by official hooks:

| Event | Flags | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `UserPromptSubmit`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure` | `--heartbeat` (async) | the session is actively working |
| `SessionStart` | `--idle` | quiet on the splash screen |
| `Stop`, `StopFailure`, `SessionEnd` | `--idle` | the turn/session ended |
| `PermissionRequest` | `--idle` (async) | the agent waits on the user — not executing |
| `PreToolUse` (`AskUserQuestion` matcher) | `--idle` (async) | the question tool is asking the user |
| `Notification` (`elicitation_dialog`, `elicitation_url_dialog`) | `--idle` (async) | MCP elicitation is waiting on the user |
| `PermissionDenied` | `--heartbeat` (async) | denied → control returns to the agent |
| `Notification` (`idle_prompt` matcher) | `--idle` (async) | bounded quiet after a paused/idle stretch |
| `SessionStart` | `--watch` | seeds the transcript watcher (`watchPaths` — the instant Esc path) |
| `FileChanged` | `--interrupt-check` (async) | any transcript write; an Esc-interrupt write quiets + flips instantly |

No hook fires when the user presses **Esc** to interrupt a turn (Stop skips
interrupts, StopFailure is API-errors only), but the transcript records the
interrupt (`[Request interrupted by user]` as the newest turn event), so the
hide works in three layers:

1. **Instant:** the `SessionStart` hook returns `watchPaths` naming its
   transcript — Claude Code's filesystem watcher then fires `FileChanged`
   the moment the interrupt-marker write lands, no matter what wrote it.
   The hook checks the ledger + transcript tail: busy + interrupted → idle
   mark + instant-paint flip, all within milliseconds of the Esc press.
2. **Self-heal:** the statusline runs the same check on every refresh tick
   while the ledger says busy — the belt for sessions whose watcher is cold
   (no `SessionStart` seed yet) — and also writes the idle mark itself.
3. **Fast typist:** a heartbeat that hits Enter before either layer healed
   the ledger verifies the suspicious busy mark against the transcript
   first (a stale interrupt is a "lie") and still counts the Enter as a
   real transition — so the re-Enter card paints instantly too.

Rules: sessions are independent (two Claude windows never wake each other
up), a busy mark goes stale after 15 minutes (a crashed session can never pin
the card), and every REAL busy↔idle transition repaints INSTANTLY: the hook
first marks the ledger, then flips the stored statusline command between two
behavior-identical variants (a trailing ` --wf`) — Claude Code re-runs the
statusline the moment the command changes in settings.json, skipping its
300 ms update debounce, so Enter→card, question→hide, and answer→card all
land within a few hundred milliseconds instead of at the next refresh tick.
The 2-second `refreshInterval` remains as the safety net. The hook writes
only the `statusLine.command` string (read-modify-write of settings.json),
the suffix is inert for rendering, and a re-run of init accepts either
variant. A missing ledger (pre-ledger install) falls back to the legacy
always-busy panel so the news keeps working without a re-run of init.

## Install & migration

`npx waitfeed init` stages the self-contained bundles into `~/.claude/waitfeed/`
and writes `statusLine` + the hook set into `~/.claude/settings.json`
(idempotent — re-running never duplicates entries).

**Upgrading from v1.2-era installs:** re-run `npx waitfeed init` once to
receive the full hook set, `refreshInterval`, and the quiet-when-idle
behavior. Without the re-run the panel keeps working in legacy
always-on mode.

## Development

- Source: `claude/src/` — `statusline.ts` (runner glue), `statusline-state.ts`
  (pure parse/width/busy decisions), `activity.ts` (ledger),
  `flip.ts` (instant-paint command flip), `interrupt.ts` (Esc-interrupt
  detector), `watch.ts` (transcript-watcher seed), `scheduler.ts`
  (`--cycle` fetch pipeline + `--heartbeat`/`--idle` ledger writers +
  `--watch`/`--interrupt-check` instant-Esc modes),
  `stdin.ts` (shared stdin collector).
- Build: `npm run build:claude` from the repo root bundles into
  `claude/dist/*.mjs` (self-contained; the staged directory needs no
  node_modules beside it).
- Tests: `tests/claude.test.ts` (pure logic), `tests/claude-bundle.test.ts`
  (E2E via plain Node), `tests/cli.test.ts` (init/idempotency).

The adapter is strictly observational: it never modifies prompts, tools, or
agent behavior, prints nothing when idle, and every entry point exits 0.
